questions.prompt: Selam has bought paint and brushes. What is she going to do? Choose the best sentence.
options: She is going to paint her room.
She going to paint her room.
She is go to paint her room.
She are going to paint her room.
questions.explanation: 'going to' for a plan needs be + going to + base verb. 'She' takes 'is', so 'She is going to paint her room.'

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly describes a daily habit?
options: My brother brushing his teeth every morning.
My brother brush his teeth every morning.
My brother brushes his teeth every morning.
My brother are brush his teeth every morning.
questions.explanation: 'My brother' is third person singular, so the verb adds -es: brushes. The simple present is used for daily habits.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'A river is ____ than a small stream.'
questions.explanation: 'Wide' is a short adjective, so the comparative adds -r: wider. We use 'than' to compare two things.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The Blue Nile is the longest river in the country.
The Blue Nile is the longer river in the country.
The Blue Nile is longest river in the country.
The Blue Nile is the most long river in the country.
questions.explanation: 'Long' is a short adjective, so the superlative is 'longest', and superlatives always take 'the': the longest river.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Last Sunday the children ____ a kite in the field.'
questions.explanation: 'Fly' is an irregular verb, so its past simple is 'flew', not 'flyed'. 'Last Sunday' shows a finished past action.

questions.prompt: Your friend has a toothache. Which sentence gives good advice?
options: You should to see a dentist.
questions.explanation: After the modal 'should' we use the base verb with no 'to' and no -s: 'You should see a dentist.'

questions.prompt: Keeping yourself and your surroundings clean to stay healthy is called:
questions.explanation: 'Hygiene' means keeping yourself and your surroundings clean to stay healthy.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a countable noun?
questions.explanation: 'Banana' can be counted and made plural (one banana, two bananas), so it is countable. Rice, honey and milk are uncountable.

questions.prompt: Which first conditional sentence about tomorrow's weather is correct?
options: If it will rain tomorrow, we will stay at home.
If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
If it rains tomorrow, we stay at home.
If it rained tomorrow, we will stay at home.
questions.explanation: The first conditional is 'If + present, ... will + verb'. After 'if' we use the present tense, so 'If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.'

questions.prompt: Your bag looks heavy. Which sentence is a polite offer of help?
options: I am carrying it for you.
I will carry it for you.
questions.explanation: We use 'will' for an offer or a decision made at the moment of speaking: 'I will carry it for you.'

questions.prompt: Rewrite 'The countryside is quieter than the city' using 'as ... as'. Choose the best option.
options: The city is as quiet as the countryside.
The city is not as quiet as the countryside.
The city is not quieter as the countryside.
The city is so quiet as the countryside.
questions.explanation: 'The countryside is quieter' means the city is less quiet. The negative 'not as ... as' shows this: 'The city is not as quiet as the countryside.'

questions.prompt: Choose the best connector: 'The town has many shops, ____ my village has only one.'
questions.explanation: 'While' shows a contrast between two different ideas. 'So', 'because' and 'therefore' show reason or result, not contrast.

questions.prompt: Which question is grammatically correct?
options: Where did the team played their match?
Where the team did play their match?
Where did the team play their match?
Where did the team playing their match?
questions.explanation: After 'did' we use the base verb (play), not the past form (played) or -ing: 'Where did the team play their match?'

questions.prompt: Make an adverb: 'The runner trained ____ for the marathon.'
questions.explanation: We need an adverb to describe how he trained. The adverb of 'serious' is 'seriously' (adjective + -ly).

questions.prompt: Complete the warning sign: '____ near the open fire.'
questions.explanation: A negative imperative is formed with 'Don't' + base verb: 'Don't play near the open fire.'

questions.prompt: Make this passive: 'People speak Amharic in many regions.' Choose the best sentence.
options: Amharic is speak in many regions.
Amharic is spoken in many regions.
questions.explanation: The present passive is 'be + past participle'. The past participle of 'speak' is 'spoken', so: 'Amharic is spoken in many regions.'

questions.prompt: Complete: 'There aren't ____ chairs in the classroom.'
questions.explanation: 'Chairs' is a countable plural noun, so we use 'many': 'There aren't many chairs.'

questions.prompt: Complete: 'My uncle has worked on the coffee farm ____ five years.'
questions.explanation: 'Five years' is a length of time, so we use 'for'. We use 'since' with a starting point such as 'since 2019'.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word to begin a set of instructions: '____, wash your hands with soap and water.'
questions.explanation: 'First' shows the opening step in a sequence of instructions. 'Finally' is the last step, while 'however' and 'although' do not show order.

questions.prompt: In a text about trade, to 'export' a product means to:
options: grow it on a small farm
sell and send it to another country
questions.explanation: 'Export' means to sell and send goods to another country, such as Ethiopia exporting coffee.

questions.prompt: Which present perfect sentence is completely correct?
options: She has wrote three letters today.
She have written three letters today.
She has write three letters today.
She has written three letters today.
questions.explanation: The present perfect is 'have/has + past participle'. 'She' takes 'has', and the past participle of 'write' is 'written'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the article correctly?
options: My father is a honest farmer.
My father is an honest farmer.
My father is the honest farmer.
questions.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a silent 'h', so the word starts with a vowel sound. We use 'an' before a vowel sound: 'an honest farmer.'

questions.prompt: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?
options: Each of the students have a notebook.
Each of the students are having a notebook.
Each of the students has a notebook.
Each of the students have got notebooks.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it takes a singular verb: 'Each of the students has a notebook.' The phrase 'of the students' does not change the verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'The athlete ____ won the race is from Ethiopia.'
questions.explanation: We use 'who' to refer to a person. 'Which' is for things, 'whose' shows possession, and 'where' refers to a place.

questions.prompt: Report this: She said, 'I am tired.' Choose the best option.
options: She said that she is tired.
She said that she was tired.
She said that I was tired.
She said that she are tired.
questions.explanation: In reported speech the present 'am' moves back to the past 'was', and 'I' changes to 'she': 'She said that she was tired.'

questions.prompt: Choose the best phrasal verb: 'Please ____ the lights before you leave the room.'
questions.explanation: 'Turn off' means to stop a machine or light from working. 'Turn off the lights' means to switch them off.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses 'its' / 'it's' correctly?
options: The dog wagged it's tail happily.
The dog wagged its' tail happily.
The dog wagged its tail happily.
The dog wagged it is tail happily.
questions.explanation: 'Its' is the possessive form (belonging to it). 'It's' means 'it is'. The dog owns the tail, so we use 'its'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'While I ____ my homework, the lights went out.'
questions.explanation: The past continuous (was/were + -ing) shows an action in progress when another action interrupted it: 'While I was doing my homework, the lights went out.'

questions.prompt: Choose the correct preposition: 'The pen is ____ the table and the book.'
questions.explanation: We use 'between' for two things and 'among' for three or more. Here there are two things (the table and the book), so 'between' is correct.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct noun form: 'The athlete trained with great ____.'
questions.explanation: After 'great' we need a noun. The noun form of 'determine' is 'determination'. The others are a verb, an adjective and an adverb.

questions.prompt: Add the correct question tag: 'They have finished the project, ____'
questions.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag, and the tag repeats the auxiliary. The auxiliary is 'have', so the tag is 'haven't they?'

questions.prompt: Which health-advice sentence is completely correct in grammar?
options: If you want to stay healthy, you should to eat a balanced diet.
If you will want to stay healthy, you should eat a balanced diet.
If you want to stay healthy, you should eats a balanced diet.
If you want to stay healthy, you should eat a balanced diet.
questions.explanation: After 'if' we use the present tense (want), and after the modal 'should' we use the base verb with no 'to': 'should eat'. So the last option is correct.

questions.topic: Mixed tenses (present perfect and past simple)
questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that is completely correct.
options: I have met him last year when he has visited our school.
I met him last year when he visited our school.
I have met him last year when he visited our school.
I met him last year when he has visited our school.
questions.explanation: Both actions happened at a finished past time ('last year'), so both verbs use the past simple: 'I met him last year when he visited our school.'

questions.prompt: Which sentence about growing rice is grammatically correct?
options: Much rice are grown in the lowland areas.
Many rice is grown in the lowland areas.
A lot of rice is grown in the lowland areas.
A lot of rice are grown in the lowland areas.
questions.explanation: 'Rice' is uncountable, so it takes 'is' and works with 'a lot of' (not 'many'). The passive needs 'grown': 'A lot of rice is grown...'

questions.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: My sister who lives in Adama is a nurse.
My sister, who lives in Adama, is a nurse.
My sister who lives in Adama, is a nurse.
My sister, who lives in Adama is a nurse.
questions.explanation: The clause 'who lives in Adama' gives extra, non-essential information, so it is set off by a pair of commas on both sides.

questions.prompt: Read: 'Although the medicine was bitter, the patient took it without complaining, for she was determined to recover.' What does 'determined' suggest about the patient?
options: She was afraid of the medicine.
She had a strong wish to get better.
She did not care about her health.
She refused to take the medicine.
questions.explanation: Being 'determined to recover' and taking the bitter medicine without complaining shows she had a strong wish to get better.
